speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at the history of the industry, the open source version of everything has been much safer.
zh: 如果你回顾这个行业的历史,所有东西的开源版本都要安全得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the internet and Linux were far safer than Windows.
zh: 所以互联网和 Linux 远比 Windows 安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, by a lot.
zh: 程度上差很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The safest thing for the world is that there's not one AI to rule them all.
zh: 对世界来说最安全的事情是,没有一个统治一切的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That there's AI for everybody.
zh: 而是每个人都有 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that open source is basically the best path towards that goal.
zh: 我认为开源基本上是实现那个目标的最佳路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably the single most important policy issue around AI.
zh: 这可能是围绕 AI 最重要的单一政策问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like we're at a stable equilibrium in the market, but the truth is the AI market is probably less than 3% penetrated.
zh: 感觉我们处于市场中一个稳定的平衡状态,但事实是 AI 市场可能被渗透了不到 3%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should AI be open?
zh: AI 应该是开源的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Theo Jaffe and Sofia Puccini are joined by Ben Horowitz to discuss the battle over open-source AI, why he believes open models are essential to innovation and national security, and what the future of AI competition means for startups, frontier labs, and the broader technology ecosystem.
zh: Theo Jaffe 和 Sofia Puccini 与 Ben Horowitz 一起讨论关于开源 AI 的战斗、为什么他认为开源模型对创新和国家安全至关重要,以及 AI 竞争的未来对初创公司、前沿实验室和更广泛的技术生态系统意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are live with Ben Horowitz of Andreessen Horowitz, who needs no introduction.
zh: 我们正在与 Andreessen Horowitz 的 Ben Horowitz 直播连线,他不需要任何介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we'll just dive right into it.
zh: 所以我们将直接进入正题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ben, welcome back to MTS.
zh: Ben,欢迎回到 MTS。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Happy to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much has happened in the world of open source, open weights in the last couple of weeks.
zh: 在过去几周里,开源和开放权重的世界里发生了很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's gotten real.
zh: 变得真刀真枪了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some drama going on.
zh: 正在发生一些抓马。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an open letter released by NVIDIA today called Open Weights in American AI Leadership, signed by many companies, including Andreessen Horowitz.
zh: NVIDIA 今天发布了一封名为《开放权重与美国 AI 领导力》的公开信,由包括 Andreessen Horowitz 在内的许多公司签署。

speaker: Unknown
en: So can you tell us a little bit about the intent behind this letter and what you hope to achieve from it?
zh: 那么你能告诉我们一点这封信背后的意图以及你希望从中实现什么吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think that it's probably the single most important policy issue around AI that's kind of currently going on.
zh: 是的,所以我认为这可能是围绕 AI 的最重要的单一政策问题,也是当前正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, the kind of battle is between kind of almost an anti-competitive stance guised in a kind of safety cloak is kind of what we ought to be doing.
zh: 而且,你知道的,这种战斗是在,几乎是一种伪装在安全外衣下的反竞争立场,是我们应该做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you look at why is open source important, and there's many reasons.
zh: 所以如果你看看为什么开源很重要,有很多原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first will just start academia.
zh: 首先就从学术界开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Academia is completely out of the AI game if there's no open source.
zh: 如果没有开源,学术界就完全出局了,无法参与 AI 游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that goes away.
zh: 那就没了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think secondly, we just had a really interesting security incident with OpenAI hacking into Hugging Face.
zh: 我认为其次,我们刚刚经历了一个非常有趣的安全事件,OpenAI 黑入了 Hugging Face。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the only way Hugging Face was able to prevent it, because the proprietary models had guardrails which prevented them from doing security tasks, was to use an open source model.
zh: 而 Hugging Face 能够阻止它的唯一方法,因为专有模型有阻止它们执行安全任务的护栏,是使用开源模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the important point there is you can't actually ban open source, of course.
zh: 我认为重要的一点是你当然无法真正禁止开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's out there.
zh: 它就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a file.
zh: 它是一个文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's on the internet.
zh: 它在互联网上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have no way of doing that.
zh: 我们没有任何办法做到那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it reminds me of years ago when I was at Netscape, they tried to ban cryptography.
zh: 这让我想起多年前我在 Netscape 的时候,他们试图禁止密码学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the math is out there.
zh: 数学就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to ban it.
zh: 你不会禁掉它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not actually possible.
zh: 这其实是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can prevent the good guys from using it.
zh: 但你可以阻止好人使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what would happen, I think, in the case of an open source ban is, you know, the threats would be, well, you can't work with the U.S. government if you use open source or you can't do this.
zh: 而那就是会发生的事情,我认为,在开源禁令的情况下,你知道的,威胁会是,好吧,如果你使用开源你就不能与美国政府合作,或者你不能做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a company like Hugging Face would not be able to actually use the product.
zh: 所以像 Hugging Face 这样的公司将无法真正使用该产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that, you know, would be bad.
zh: 所以,你知道的,那会很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then kind of getting into...
zh: 但然后就进入……

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like if you look at the history of the industry, the open source version of everything has been much safer.
zh: 就像如果你回顾这个行业的历史,所有东西的开源版本都要安全得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the internet and Linux were far safer than Windows, like by a lot.
zh: 所以互联网和 Linux 远比 Windows 安全,程度差很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And why is that?
zh: 而那是为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, because the whole community could work on the safety problems as opposed to just a company and particularly a monopoly company that, you know, like you can't.
zh: 好吧,因为整个社区都可以致力于解决安全问题,而不是仅仅一家公司,特别是一家垄断公司,你知道的,就像你无法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if Windows has a million security bugs, there's nothing we can do about it because it was a monopoly at the time, right?
zh: 即使 Windows 有一百万个安全漏洞,我们也对此无能为力,因为它当时是垄断的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that, you know, that's a very difficult position for the world to be in.
zh: 所以,你知道的,那对世界来说是一个非常困难的处境。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at, now, the argument against open AI or AI being open source is, oh, well, nobody understands how the weights work.
zh: 如果你看看,现在,反对开源 AI 或 AI 开源的论点是,哦,好吧,没有人理解这些权重是如何工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, it's not like people could inspect it.
zh: 所以,你知道,这不像人们可以检查它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But...
zh: 但是...

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it better to not see the whites if that's the case?
zh: 如果是那样的话,为什么看不到这些白心会更好?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in reality, if you look at the really tough problems that we have safety-wise, the toughest being reward hacking currently.
zh: 我认为在现实中,如果你看看我们在安全方面面临的真正棘手的问题,目前最难的是奖励黑客行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, Anthropic has not solved it.
zh: 而且显然,Anthropic 还没有解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, OpenAI has not solved it because we just had these incidents.
zh: 显然,OpenAI 也没有解决它,因为我们刚刚就发生了这些事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, shouldn't the whole world be able to look at, okay, how are the weights moving?
zh: 那么,整个世界不应该能够看到,好的,权重是如何变化的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it that guardrails don't prevent the reward hack?
zh: 为什么护栏不能防止奖励黑客行为?

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe somebody can come up with an answer, somebody who doesn't work for one of the proprietary labs who are much more focused on, you know, obviously keeping ahead on the benchmarks and getting the money and all that kind of thing.
zh: 也许有人能想出一个答案,某个不在那些专有实验室工作的人,那些实验室显然更专注于,你知道,在基准测试上保持领先、拿到钱以及诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, what if the whole community could work on it?
zh: 你知道,如果整个社区都能来研究它会怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like really, really important, I think, to safety in general.
zh: 所以我认为,这对整体安全来说真的、真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, kind of finally, the safest thing for the world is that there's not one AI to rule them all, that there's kind of AI for everybody.
zh: 然后,你知道,最后,对世界来说最安全的事情是,没有一个统治所有 AI 的 AI,而是每个人都有 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that open source is basically the best path, you know, kind of towards that goal.
zh: 而且我认为开源基本上是实现那个目标的最佳路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Jensen made a Twitter account basically to publish this.
zh: 所以 Jensen 基本上是注册了一个 Twitter 账号来发布这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that I think speaks to the significance of where we are right now that he was like, okay, it now is the time to, you know, speak out about this and get all of these companies to like, you know, co-sign it.
zh: 所以我认为这说明了我们目前所处位置的重要性,他觉得,好的,现在是时候了,你知道,公开谈论这个并让所有这些公司,你知道,联署它。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think are some of the risks right now from like a government action perspective on open source?
zh: 你认为目前从政府行动的角度来看,开源有哪些风险?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, look, I think there's a huge push with a lot of money behind it, you know, particularly from Anthropic to ban open source.
zh: 嗯,听着,我认为有一股巨大的推动力,背后有大量的资金,你知道,特别是来自 Anthropic 要禁止开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that it is kind of nefarious from my point of view, but, you know, whatever their motivation is, they do have...
zh: 我认为从我的角度来看这有点恶意,但是,你知道,不管他们的动机是什么,他们确实有...

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things that happened with cryptography...
zh: 所以密码学领域发生的事情之一...

speaker: Unknown
en: is there are people who are very senior in the intelligence community who didn't understand the technological aspect of it, who pushed for banning cryptography because they wanted control.
zh: 是有一些在情报界非常资深的人,他们不理解它的技术层面,他们推动禁止密码学,因为他们想要控制权。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that it's a similar thing here where...
zh: 我认为这里的情况类似,其中...

speaker: Unknown
en: It just feels like more control if you can stop some kind of AI.
zh: 如果你能阻止某种 AI,感觉就像是更多的控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: But those are very powerful forces in the conversation right now.
zh: 但那些是当前对话中非常强大的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that there is certainly a kind of pretty strong community pushing for the banning of open source.
zh: 而且我认为确实存在一个相当强大的社区推动禁止开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why this letter was so important.
zh: 所以这就是为什么这封信如此重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why it's so great that...
zh: 这就是为什么...如此棒的是

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, not just Jensen, but Elon, Satya, Sam all supported it.
zh: 你知道,不仅仅是 Jensen,而且 Elon、Satya、Sam 都支持它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just think it's very obviously the right answer for safety, the right answer for America.
zh: 而且我只是认为这非常明显是对安全的正确答案,对美国的正确答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it would be a real shame if we, you know, kind of shot ourselves in the foot on this.
zh: 如果我们,你知道,在这件事上搬起石头砸自己的脚,那就太可惜了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, another angle that many people talk about with respect to open source is China and national security, as opposed to like AI safety stuff.
zh: 嗯,许多人在谈到开源时谈论的另一个角度是中国和国家安全,而不是 AI 安全之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some people say, you know, it's a national security risk for so many American startups to be dependent on like infrastructure that comes from China, you know, in the event that, for example, China decided to cut everything off and stop releasing better open source models.
zh: 有些人说,你知道,这么多美国初创公司依赖来自中国的基础设施,这是一种国家安全风险,你知道,如果例如,中国决定切断一切并停止向美国公司发布更好的开源模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: to American companies or perhaps they could you know in an AI future make these open source models like sleeper agents basically or you can think of all kinds of things that they could do
zh: 或者也许他们可以你知道的在未来的 AI 中把这些开源模型基本上变成潜伏智能体,或者你能想到他们能做的各种事情

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, as could a Chinese national working for Anthropic or OpenAI or, you know, SpaceX, right?
zh: 是的,我的意思是,一个在 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 或,你知道,SpaceX 工作的中国公民也可能如此,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's not like these Chinese nationals cannot be activated by the Chinese government.
zh: 就好像,并不是说这些中国公民不能被中国政府激活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we've seen that.
zh: 就像,我们已经看到过那样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, like, if that's a threat, like, I think that's just a general threat, not specific to open source AI.
zh: 所以,像那样,如果那是一个威胁,我认为那只是一个普遍的威胁,并非开源 AI 特有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nothing against Chinese nationals.
zh: 而且对中国公民没有任何意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: We love them.
zh: 我们爱他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're great for our country and so forth.
zh: 他们对我们的国家很棒等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, like, if you're worried about that...
zh: 但是,就像,如果你担心那个...

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, you ought to be worried about it.
zh: 你知道,你就应该担心它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the more likely way, I think, would be that kind of spy activation.
zh: 就像,我认为更可能的方式会是那种间谍激活。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, look, it's open source.
zh: 但是,听着,它是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, if they stop making it, like, we've still got the last code base, we can train up the model, we can, you know, we can learn from it.
zh: 所以,如果他们停止制作它,就像,我们仍然拥有最后的代码库,我们可以训练模型,我们可以,你知道,我们可以从中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the meanwhile, there's, I mean, the great thing about open is it's open.
zh: 同时,我的意思是,开放的好处就在于它是开放的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, look, we need to build our own open source products here.
zh: 而且,你知道,听着,我们需要在这里构建我们自己的开源产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thinking Machines is doing a good job of that.
zh: Thinking Machines 在这方面做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm thinking...
zh: 我在想...

speaker: Unknown
en: France, you know, Mistral's doing a good job of that.
zh: 法国,你知道,Mistral 在这方面做得不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, like, we need to keep pushing the technology forward, the open technology, so that, look, it needs to be available everywhere for everyone.
zh: 所以,我们需要不断推动技术向前发展,推动开放技术,因为,你看,它需要为所有地方的每个人提供。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, like, we can't be held hostage by, like, the worst scenario is there ends up being a monopoly in AI.
zh: 而且,我们不能被当作人质,最坏的情况是 AI 领域最终出现垄断。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think it's fairly obvious how dangerous that could be and how powerful that company would be and what a national security risk that would be.
zh: 我的意思是,我认为这相当明显那会是多么危险,那家公司会有多么强大,以及那会构成什么样的国家安全风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've already seen a glimpse of it, right, with Anthropic saying, like, I don't care who got elected in the U.S.
zh: 我们已经瞥见了一斑,对吧,Anthropic 说着,比如,我不在乎谁在美国当选了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care about the government.
zh: 我不在乎政府。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care about the Department of War.
zh: 我不在乎战争部。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not going to work with you.
zh: 我们不会和你们合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in charge.
zh: 我们说了算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you look at that, you go...
zh: 所以你看着这个,你会觉得...

speaker: Unknown
en: okay, that seems like a much bigger national security risk than the kinds of little holes people are trying to poke in the open source story.
zh: 好吧,这看起来比人们试图在开源叙事中戳破的那些小漏洞要大得多的国家安全风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just think it's very, very important that this technology proliferate and not be kept contained in a single company.
zh: 所以我只是认为这项技术能够扩散,而不是被限制在一家公司内部,这是非常、非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, definitely.
zh: 是的,绝对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have kind of become a little more defenders of distillation recently.
zh: 所以我们最近在某种程度上变得更像是蒸馏的捍卫者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we talk about how distillation is not actually illegal.
zh: 所以我们谈论蒸馏实际上如何并不是非法的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the labs are still paying API prices to use the models.
zh: 许多实验室仍然在支付 API 价格来使用模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what are your thoughts?
zh: 那么你的想法是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think it's part of a healthy competitive landscape?
zh: 你认为它是健康竞争格局的一部分吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked to Aaron Levy earlier about this, and he was like...
zh: 我们之前和 Aaron Levy 谈过这个,他当时说...

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, how can Anthropic, like, just take everyone's training data without paying them at all, but when other labs pay them, it's distillation, it needs to be banned?
zh: 你知道的,Anthropic 怎么能,就像,直接拿走每个人的训练数据却完全不付钱给他们,但是当其他实验室付钱给他们时,这就是蒸馏,就需要被禁止?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I actually agree with Aaron, and I think that's right.
zh: 是的,我其实同意 Aaron 的看法,我认为那是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, from a legal standpoint, the outputs of AI models are not copyright, and they don't fall under copyright law.
zh: 比如,从法律角度来看,AI 模型的输出不受版权保护,它们不属于版权法的范畴。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the only thing it could be is a terms of service violation.
zh: 所以它唯一可能构成的只是服务条款违规。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, look, I think generally that's right.
zh: 但是,你看,我认为总体上是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Anthropic just paid $1.5 billion for stealing everybody's books, including mine, by the way.
zh: 你知道,Anthropic 刚刚花了 15 亿美元来偷走所有人的书,顺便说一下,包括我的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They trained on MacBook and I joined that class action lawsuit.
zh: 他们在 MacBook 上进行了训练,我加入了那起集体诉讼。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, not to say, look, I'm for training them out, building a statistical model of the things we know.
zh: 所以,你知道,不是要说,看,我支持把它们训练出来,建立一个关于我们所知事物的统计模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's generally good for the world and so forth as long as you don't violate the copyright and reproduce the original work.
zh: 我认为这通常对世界是有益的等等,只要你不侵犯版权并复制原始作品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the same – yeah, like I think distillation is generally good for the world.
zh: 而且我认为同样的——是的,就像我认为蒸馏通常对世界是有益的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think they're going to have a very hard time stopping it for many reasons.
zh: 我也认为由于许多原因,他们将很难阻止它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, they have theories on how they're going to stop it, but I'm not sure that those are going to succeed, so we'll see.
zh: 是的,他们有关于如何阻止它的理论,但我不确定那些是否会成功,所以我们拭目以待。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think distillation is good and like the whole idea that we're stealing –

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, because I think that all the American labs have kind of built their businesses on proprietary models, and there's a lot kind of that becomes, and they have to kind of afford the GPUs.
zh: 嗯,因为我认为所有美国实验室都在某种程度上基于专有模型建立了他们的业务,而且有很多随之而来的东西,他们必须得负担得起 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they need these very high valuations to keep ahead on the GPUs to keep going.
zh: 你知道,他们需要这些非常高的估值才能在 GPU 方面保持领先并继续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, because they're in the lead, you know, distillation doesn't work for them because their model is on the cutting edge.
zh: 而且,你知道的,因为他们处于领先地位,蒸馏对他们不起作用,因为他们的模型处于最前沿。

speaker: Unknown

en: And that's just how kind of the markets evolved.

en: And then, you know, number two goes open is kind of the history of the software industry.

en: I do think that we're going to see, I mean, like you said, with thinking machines, they've got, you know, they're making really good headway with their open source efforts.
zh: 我确实认为我们会看到,我的意思是,就像你说的,对于 thinking machines 来说,他们已经,你知道的,在他们的开源努力上取得了非常好的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, hopefully we'll see kind of more of that and kind of more breakthroughs, you know, on the open source side.

en: Like, so if you have more GPUs, that actually turns out to be a really big deal.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你认为我们缺少那种美国开源生态系统吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it just a different thing?
zh: 还是说它只是另一种不同的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's obviously supply chain and stuff.
zh: 我的意思是,显然有供应链之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I think there's a lot to be said for that, right?
zh: 不,我认为这有很多可以说的地方,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because, you know, as an application, so what's happened, the other thing that we haven't spoken about, like, is, well, what's the AI platform?
zh: 因为,你知道,作为一个应用,所以发生的事情是,另一件我们没有谈论过的事情,比如是,那么,AI 平台是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, so if you're an application provider, what do you build on?
zh: 而且,你知道,如果你是一个应用提供商,你在什么上面构建?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we've seen is,
zh: 而我们看到的是,

speaker: Unknown
en: it's been already fairly dangerous to build on anthropic because every time an application category starts to do well, they move into that category.
zh: 在 anthropic 之上构建已经相当危险了,因为每次一个应用类别开始做得很好时,他们就会进入那个类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they've, you know, like we've seen them do like very aggressive things where, you know, the price for the application provider is full price and then they subsidize their version of the application.
zh: 然后他们已经,你知道,就像我们看到他们做过非常激进的事情,你知道,对应用提供商的价格是全价,然后他们补贴他们自己版本的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's kind of that they've kind of fast-forwarded, I would say, the Microsoft playbook from the old days to, like, skipping the platform generation and just going straight to the monopoly generation.
zh: 所以有点像他们有点快进了,我会说,微软昔日的 playbook,就像,跳过了平台这一代,直接进入了垄断这一代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're an application provider, like, okay, how can I safely build on a proprietary model if that company is going to come attack me and then charge me much more than they're charging themselves to do the same thing?
zh: 所以如果你是一个应用提供商,比如,好吧,如果那家公司要来攻击我,然后向我收取比他们自己做同样事情所收取的费用高得多的费用,我怎么能安全地在一个专有模型上构建呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so open source is kind of a way that the ecosystem gets built.
zh: 所以开源有点像是生态系统得以构建的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're building robots, for example, if you were to build your robot on Anthropic, then at some point, you know Anthropic's going to go into the robot business and put you out of business just by either cutting you off or overcharging you.
zh: 所以如果你在制造机器人,例如,如果你要在 Anthropic 之上构建你的机器人,那么在某个时刻,你知道 Anthropic 会进入机器人业务并让你破产,只需通过切断你或向你收取过高的费用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is kind of a way that their ecosystem can grow by building on the open source.
zh: 所以这有点像他们的生态系统可以通过在开源之上构建来成长的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hopefully...
zh: 并且希望……

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, a lot of our industry has grown.
zh: 顺便说一下,我们很多行业已经成长起来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of our application companies have used open source to kind of bootstrap themselves or get going or that kind of thing, and often Chinese open source, which is why it's really important to the U.S. ecosystem that we have applications, that we have embodied AI, that we have robots and all these things that we have access to that technology because the kind of other model is a monopoly model where there's one company that owns all the applications.
zh: 我们很多应用公司已经使用开源来引导自己或起步或类似的事情,而且通常是中国开源,这就是为什么对于美国生态系统来说非常重要,我们拥有应用,我们拥有具身 AI,我们拥有机器人以及所有这些我们能够访问该技术的东西,因为另一种模式是一种垄断模式,即有一家公司拥有所有的应用。

en: All the robots and all of everything.
zh: 所有的机器人和所有的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

zh: 而且你看,我不是说,我甚至不一定因为他们那样做而生气。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's their, like, that's their business approach.
zh: 这是他们的,比如,那是他们的商业方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, like, the consequences of it, if they're able to ban their competitors, is not good.
zh: 但是,比如,它的后果,如果他们能够封禁他们的竞争对手,是不好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I also...
zh: 是的,我也……

speaker: Unknown
en: worry about these, you know, very monopolistic, like centralized futures.

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like, you know, that wouldn't be so good for like a pluralistic, you know, startup ecosystem.
zh: 似乎,你知道,这对于一个多元的,你知道,初创企业生态系统来说不会那么好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's certainly their strategy, you know, and we'll see how it goes.
zh: 是的,那肯定是他们的策略,你知道,我们将看看它会如何发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that,
zh: 但我认为,

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of the best hedge against that is for like many, many companies being able to do AI, which is why the open models are powerful in that context.
zh: 对此最好的对冲有点像是许多许多公司能够做 AI,这就是为什么开源模型在那种背景下是强大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: I guess speaking of China, there's a lot of things that are like, you know, either like tariffed or I mean, we export control.
zh: 我想说到中国,有很多东西,你知道,要么被征收关税,要么我是说,我们出口管制。

en: We also tariff them like things like EVs, right?
zh: 我们也对它们征收关税,比如像 EV 这样的东西,对吧?

en: And if we had like a, you know, BYD level pricing for EVs in the U.S., that would just be like so huge.
zh: 如果我们在美国有像比亚迪那样的 EV 定价水平,那将会是如此巨大的事情。

en: Do you think there's a way that we could move towards that future?
zh: 你认为有一种方法可以让我们朝着那个未来迈进吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what would have to what would it take to get to that?

en: Well, I think that, you know, with BYD in particular, there are a lot of subsidies from the Chinese government that enable them to achieve this amazing pricing.
zh: 嗯,我认为,你知道,特别是比亚迪,有大量来自中国政府的补贴使他们能够实现这个惊人的定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of it is a kind of a – well, so kind of getting into manufacturing.
zh: 而且其中很多有点像是一种——那么,有点像进入制造业。

speaker: Unknown
en: invented so much of manufacturing and then kind of forgot what we knew.

speaker: Unknown
en: So like if you go back to, we won World War II based on our superior manufacturing capability.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then like over the next whatever 100 years, we forgot to hold that.
zh: 然后在接下来的无论 100 年里,我们忘记了保持这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to rebuild that capability and manufacturing has changed and is becoming much more automated, much more kind of AI-centric.
zh: 我们需要重建这种能力,而且制造业已经改变并且正在变得更加自动化,更加以 AI 为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think as we kind of build into the second, or you call it the third industrial revolution, that being able to be competitive on manufacturing by building automated factories and so forth, similar to what Elon has been able to do at Tesla and in the Gigafactory and so forth, is going to be the way that we get to competitiveness there for sure.
zh: 所以我认为,随着我们有点像进入第二次,或者你称之为第三次工业革命,能够通过构建自动化工厂等等在制造业上具有竞争力,类似于 Elon 在 Tesla 和 Gigafactory 等等能够做到的那样,将是我们肯定在那里获得竞争力的途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

zh: 我认为，你知道，美国现在这方面动静不多，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's just really important.
zh: 我认为这真的非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at the...

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 尤其是美国开源的缺乏，是的。

en: In the long run, what exactly is the incentive for a business to release open source models, especially if they're a foundation lab and most of their business is making the models, which are very expensive?
zh: 从长远来看，一家企业发布开源模型的确切动机到底是什么，特别是如果它们是一家基础实验室，而且它们的大部分业务就是制作这些非常昂贵的模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think that, I mean, this is where, like, I'm glad you both are pro-distillation, because I think that's an important equation.
zh: 是的，所以我认为，我的意思是，正是在这一点上，就像，我很高兴你们两位都支持蒸馏，因为我认为这是一个重要的等式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But look, I think that there's different business, like, I think the business model of selling, serving the model at a very high premium doesn't work if you're open source, but there's other things, you know, particularly, like, one of the things we already know is that, you know, for an enterprise in a B2B context,
zh: 但是你看，我认为存在不同的商业（模式），比如，我认为以非常高的溢价出售、提供模型的商业模式在开源的情况下是行不通的，但是还有其他事情，你知道，特别是，就像，我们已经知道的一件事是，你知道，对于在 B2B 环境中的企业来说，

speaker: Unknown
en: A really well post-trained, kind of less powerful, smaller model works often better for a business task than like a large, you know, kind of a large proprietary model and is much cheaper as well.
zh: 一个后训练得非常好的、算力弱一点的、更小的模型，在商业任务上的表现通常比像一个大型专有模型这样的大型模型更好，而且也便宜得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So cheaper, faster.
zh: 所以更便宜、更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: and gets you their answer.

en: So I think that it would be more like a kind of a Palantir-looking business model than it would be an Anthropocene-looking business model for a company.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, true also on the consumer side, you know, we've seen on consumer, like, the use case really, really matters.
zh: 然后呢，你知道，在消费端也是如此，你知道，我们看到在消费端，就像，用例真的、真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so kind of tuning a model for that kind of thing can really work.
zh: 因此为那种情况进行模型调优是确实可以奏效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that open source models are currently a threat to the business model of large closed source foundation model developers?
zh: 你认为开源模型目前是对大型闭源基础模型开发者的商业模式的威胁吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But also like when you compare Kimmy to Fable or Sol, there's definitely areas where Fable and Sol are just way better and people will pay for them anyway.
zh: 但同时，就像当你比较 Kimmy 和 Fable 或 Sol 时，肯定有一些领域 Fable 和 Sol 就是好得多，人们无论如何都会为它们买单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I don't think anybody's a threat, a real kind of current threat to anybody else's business right now, like in that we're so early in the market.

en: So the thing that's very deceptive about AI is because the market is so much larger than any other market we've seen prior, that it feels like...

speaker: Unknown
en: okay, we're kind of at a stable equilibrium in the market.

en: But the truth is the AI market is probably less than 3% penetrated.
zh: 但事实是 AI 市场的渗透率可能不到 3%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so everybody's going to grow.
zh: 所以每个人都会增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?

en: Like when DeepSeq came out, it was a DeepSeq moment, and oh my gosh, and this is the end of Anthropic and OpenAI and all that.

speaker: Unknown
en: And nothing changed.
zh: 然后什么都没变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like nothing changed.
zh: 就像什么都没变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zero.
zh: 零。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because, but DeepSeq is more valuable, and Anthropic's more valuable, and OpenAI is more valuable.
zh: 而那是因为，但是 DeepSeq 更有价值了，Anthropic 更有价值了，OpenAI 也更有价值了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they all agree.
zh: 你知道的，他们都同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And SpaceX is more valuable.
zh: 而且 SpaceX 也更有价值了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that at this stage of the market, everything is going to grow a lot.
zh: 我认为在市场的这个阶段，一切都会大幅增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nobody's going to pounce on other people's market share in a way that is so material that it's going to, like, cripple them.
zh: 而且没有人会以一种极其实质性的、足以像削弱他们那样的方式去抢夺其他人的市场份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

en: Now, someday...

en: When we get to some kind of equilibria in the market and there's so much share to go around and then you're fighting each other for share, then these things may come into play.

speaker: Unknown
en: But for right now, I don't think so.
